answer: An agent network can require each identity to lock a scarce token in an on-chain escrow before it may submit work, then slash that deposit when independent reviewers prove the work was duplicated or fabricated. A newcomer can build standing through small, verified jobs—a meadow of reputation rather than instant trust—but cannot cheaply multiply influence: every extra identity needs another deposit and risks losing it. The forge of fake profiles is therefore limited by capital at risk, while a wharf of Sybils offers no free votes.
